query: Why do some incidents take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: open_to_close_days_bucket
per_column.rationale: This is the resolution-duration outcome itself (how long incidents took), i.e. the very thing to be explained, not a constitutive aspect of the REASONS for delay.

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: The type of incident (email, database, vpn) is a legitimate aspect of characterizing why classes of incidents differ in delay; it is a facet of the delay-reason taxonomy (nature of the problem).

per_column.name: failure_mode
per_column.rationale: The kind of failure (outage, authentication_failure, crash) is a constitutive aspect of what goes wrong and thus of the reason an incident is hard/slow to resolve.

per_column.name: affected_component
per_column.rationale: Which component is affected (server_side, network_infrastructure, client_application) is an aspect of the problem's nature, a facet of the delay-reason characterization.

per_column.name: scope_indicator
per_column.rationale: Scope/blast radius (system_wide, individual_user) is a constitutive aspect of an incident's difficulty and a plausible facet of delay reasons.

per_column.name: assigned_at_open
per_column.rationale: Whether assignment happened at open is a process/workflow attribute that may predict delay but is not itself an aspect OF the delay reason concept.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Whether resolver matched is an operational/routing predictor of delay, not a constitutive part of the delay-reason concept.

per_column.name: assignee_id
per_column.rationale: The identity of the assignee is an external actor attribute that may correlate with delay but is not a facet of the reason itself.

per_column.name: caller_id_group
per_column.rationale: Caller identity is an external entity attribute, not a constitutive aspect of why resolution is delayed.

judge.rationale: Only four of nine columns are genuine facets of the delay-reason concept: incident_category, failure_mode, affected_component, and scope_indicator all describe the intrinsic nature of the problem. The remaining columns fail the meronymy test: open_to_close_days_bucket restates the outcome (duration) being explained; assigned_at_open, resolver_match, assignee_id, and caller_id_group are external process/actor predictors, not constitutive parts of the reason. Among the true facets, mutual exclusivity is weakened because incident_category, failure_mode, and affected_component substantially overlap (e.g., 'vpn'/'network_connectivity' category, 'connection_failure' mode, and 'network_infrastructure' component often encode the same underlying situation), so they do not cleanly carve non-overlapping aspects. Exhaustiveness is moderate: the facets cover problem-type, failure-kind, component, and scope, but omit key delay-driving aspects such as diagnostic complexity, dependency/vendor involvement, information/resource availability, and required remediation effort.
